# Autonomous resonant quantum sources with self-stabilizing allocation

1 November 2026. Proofs, executable finite-device comparisons, and preserved failures.

## Leading result

A specified finite-dimensional autonomous memory construction now has a resonant quantum syndrome source, physical self-stabilizing ownership control, and a formal positive noise-admission region. It does not require a trusted global clock or reliable ownership records. It admits sufficiently small continuing local coherent and dissipative errors on the modeled data and apparatus. The whole join received a separate internal mathematical review.

The key design change was selected by a stronger comparison, not by defending the first method. A noisy physical token beats dilute random starts in the actual two-probe model; the graph construction extends the mechanism with abort-on-contention locks and full owner-only cleanup. Native partial probes are never reset or paused merely because a lock was lost.

## What is actually specified

- Quantum source: resonant apparatus–data two-body Hamiltonians and explicitly stated onsite preparation, collective decay, and readout channels.
- Allocator: a qudit of dimension 8w+4D+10 per check and one physical qutrit per conflict edge; two-site classical ownership transitions.
- Remaining Boolean decoder machinery: its previously admitted at-most-three-site classical GKSL operations.
- Logical consumer: the specified Tanner-witness code family, ideal encoded input and ideal terminal decoder, with actual finite-depth frame and noise costs included.

Here w is check weight and D conflict degree. A qudit is not a qubit. Selective multilevel transitions, probe-coherence-preserving collective emission, reservoir purity, pumping and entropy disposal are required interfaces. The package does not derive an atomic implementation or grant these resources for free.

Kastoryano–Wolf–Eisert, Precisely timing dissipative quantum information processing, arXiv1205.0985v2 (29 Nov 2012), https://arxiv.org/pdf/1205.0985 . Actual full paper read. Time-independent dissipative initialization/timer gadgets and a dissipative measurement-based-computation construction already supply autonomously sequenced operations. Theorem1 requires a sufficient fraction of auxiliary initial excitations; conditional preparation jumps act on multiple sites, with amplitude damping. Geometric computation uses up to six-site dissipators. It does not prove a perpetually refreshed parity service with continuing arbitrary apparatus noise from the exact restricted two-body-Hamiltonian/onsite-decay alphabet. Sequential dissipative clocks are prior; the requested physical/noise admission is not supplied by this theorem.

Earlier inspected Kerckhoff et al. arXiv1102.3143v1 already gives continuously refreshed physical parity relays and Raman feedback using CW optical networks, but through ideal reduced input-output limits and without general noisy-apparatus scalable admission. Reiter et al. NatCommun8,1822 (2017), https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-017-01895-5.pdf explicitly treats several auxiliary imperfections in a finite repetition-code reservoir-engineering model. Neither should be dismissed as merely a noiseless classical controller; neither is a complete same-resource dominator.

For a fixed cache branch c_a in each cell, local dimension is 2w (g, w-1 intermediates, e, w-1 dumps); pair Hamiltonian dimension (2w)^2. Both g/e endpoints remain in the four-dimensional low subspace. All intermediate/dump states are eliminated by the EXACT finite-matrix Feshbach/Schur complement H_LL-H_LH H_HH^-1 H_HL at E=0. Also computed real diagonals with the actual endpoint/dump no-jump decay terms. This is not an effective-Lindbladian or dynamical-gap theorem. Code: conditional_schur.py.
Checks are Z^w and X^w on the same EVEN number of data sites, so they commute. A joint (+,+) stabilizer state selects scalar apparatus blocks after exact prefix gauge. Tested cache branches (0,0),(1,0),(1,1), including cold gg and excited ee endpoints in the retained basis. Leading effect is effectively cache-label independent.

For wrong cache branches, off-diagonal bright drives remain approximately 2J. One-wrong and both-wrong configurations therefore encounter real detuning, not just harmless common Stark energy. Independent onsite counterterms cannot remove the mixed combination E_gg-E_ge-E_eg+E_ee. Ordinary off-resonant drive reasoning suggests service suppression ~J*(J/detuning)^2, but no actual full Liouvillian gap is asserted.
The leading term is the signed-square (two overlapping virtual excursions) frustration cost. A pi-flux square changes fourth-order ground energy by 2g^4/Delta^3 relative to the commuting square.
